title: Active/Passive & Narration
intro: Two transformation skills sit here. Voice change converts an active sentence (the doer acts) into the passive (the action is done to the subject) and back. Narration converts direct speech (exact words in quotes) into indirect/reported speech. Both follow mechanical rules — swap subject and object, change the verb form, shift the tense and pronouns. Learn the rules once and apply them step by step.

items.name: Active → Passive
items.formula: object + be + past participle (+ by + doer)

items.name: Reported speech
items.formula: remove quotes; shift tense back one step; change pronouns

topics.name: Active to Passive
topics.details: To make a passive: move the object to the front, add the correct form of 'be' in the same tense, then the past participle of the main verb, and put the doer after 'by'. Keep the tense.

solved.solution: A letter is written by Ram.
The wall was painted by her.

solved.problem: Make passive: "They have completed the project."
solved.solution: The project has been completed by them.
You will be helped by him.

unsolved.problem: Make passive: "The cat caught a mouse."
unsolved.answer: A mouse was caught by the cat.

unsolved.problem: Make passive: "People speak English here."
unsolved.answer: English is spoken here.

unsolved.problem: Make passive: "She is writing a novel."
unsolved.answer: A novel is being written by her.

unsolved.problem: Make passive: "They will build a bridge."
unsolved.answer: A bridge will be built by them.

unsolved.problem: Make passive: "He has eaten the apple."
unsolved.answer: The apple has been eaten by him.

topics.name: Passive to Active
topics.details: Reverse the process: find the doer (after 'by'), make it the subject, drop the 'be' helper, and use the correct active verb form in the same tense. If no doer is named, supply a sensible subject.

solved.problem: Make active: "A letter is written by Ram."
Make active: "The wall was painted by her."
Make active: "The project has been completed by them."
Make active: "English is spoken here." (no doer)

unsolved.problem: Make active: "A mouse was caught by the cat."
unsolved.answer: The cat caught a mouse.

unsolved.problem: Make active: "You will be helped by him."
unsolved.answer: He will help you.

unsolved.problem: Make active: "The apple has been eaten by him."
unsolved.answer: He has eaten the apple.

unsolved.problem: Make active: "A novel is being written by her."
unsolved.answer: She is writing a novel.

unsolved.problem: Make active: "The bridge will be built by them."
unsolved.answer: They will build a bridge.

topics.name: Direct to Indirect Speech
topics.details: To report a statement: remove the quotation marks, add 'that', shift the tense one step back, and change the pronouns to match the speaker. Time/place words shift too.

solved.solution: He said that he was busy.

solved.problem: Report: She said, "I will come tomorrow."
solved.solution: She said that she would come the next day.
They said that they had finished.

solved.problem: Report: He said, "I bought it yesterday."
solved.solution: He said that he had bought it the previous day.

unsolved.problem: Report: She said, "I am tired."
unsolved.answer: She said that she was tired.

unsolved.problem: Report: He said, "I can swim."
unsolved.answer: He said that he could swim.

unsolved.problem: Report: They said, "We are leaving now."
unsolved.answer: They said that they were leaving then.

unsolved.problem: Report: She said, "I saw him here."
unsolved.answer: She said that she had seen him there.

unsolved.problem: Report: He said, "I will help you."
unsolved.answer: He said that he would help me.

topics.name: Reported Questions & Commands
topics.details: Reporting questions: use 'asked' and turn the question into statement order (no inversion, no question mark). Yes/no questions add 'if/whether'; wh-questions keep the wh-word. Commands/requests use 'told/requested' + to-infinitive.

solved.problem: Report: He said, "Where do you live?"

solved.solution: She asked if/whether I was ready.

solved.problem: Report: He said to me, "Open the door."
solved.solution: He told me to open the door.
She told me not to be late.

unsolved.problem: Report: He asked, "What is your name?"
unsolved.answer: He asked what my name was.

unsolved.problem: Report: She said, "Do you like tea?"
unsolved.answer: She asked if I liked tea.

unsolved.problem: Report: The teacher said, "Sit down."
unsolved.answer: The teacher told us to sit down.

unsolved.problem: Report: He said, "Please help me."
unsolved.answer: He requested me to help him.

unsolved.problem: Report: She said, "Don't touch it."
unsolved.answer: She told me not to touch it.

shortcuts: Passive: object + be (same tense) + past participle + by + doer.
Active: doer becomes subject; drop "be"; use the active verb in the same tense.
Reported speech: add "that", shift tense back one step, change pronouns.
Time/place shift: now→then, today→that day, here→there, this→that.
Reported questions = statement order + if/whether (yes-no) or wh-word; commands = "to"/"not to".
mistakes: Forgetting to keep the original tense in the passive be-form.
Not back-shifting the tense in reported speech.
Leaving question word order (inversion) in a reported question.
Using "said" instead of "asked/told" for questions and commands.
pyq: SSC asks one or two voice-change items and one narration item per Tier 1, in both directions. They are mechanical once the rules are memorised — apply them step by step.

flashcards.a: A letter is written by Ram
He said that he was ill

summary: Voice and narration are mechanical transformations. For the passive, front the object and use be (same tense) + past participle + by + doer; reverse it for active. For reported speech, drop the quotes, back-shift the tense, change pronouns and time words, and use asked/told with if/whether or "to" for questions and commands.
